provenance: Lane split authored by Stage-2 decision-agent (read-only) and persisted by the orchestrator. NOTE: this environment's bundled ATT&CK defines T1685='Disable or Modify Tools' and T1685.005='Clear Windows Event Logs' (T1562.001/T1070.001 not in dataset; defense-evasion tactic = 'stealth'); IDs conform to that, matching the rest of the repo and CI.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — exploitation of known CVEs and SQLi is detectable via WAF/IDS signatures, vulnerable-appliance version telemetry, and anomalous post-auth VPN sessions, but n-day exploitation of edge devices often precedes visibility
high — new .aspx files in web-root paths and w3wp.exe/IIS worker spawning cmd.exe are strong, well-covered detection signals

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
detection_candidates.rationale: high — new service creation (Event ID 7045 / registry Services key writes) pointing at unusual binaries is highly detectable

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: high — cmd.exe spawned by an IIS worker (w3wp.exe) or other web-server parent is a classic web-shell command-execution detection
high — scheduled-task creation (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational) launching a one-time batch that clears logs is a strong, anomalous signal
medium — base64-heavy .aspx content and runtime decode routines are detectable via web-content inspection and script-block/AMSI telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — vulnerable-driver loads (Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist / Sysmon driver-load) and EDR-service tampering are detectable, but BYOVD kernel action can blind the very sensor meant to see it

detection_candidates.technique_name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
detection_candidates.rationale: high — event-log clearing (Security 1102 / System 104) is a discrete, high-fidelity signal, ideally forwarded off-host before the wipe completes
high — LSASS process access with dump rights (Sysmon EID 10 / EDR credential-theft analytics) and ProcDump against lsass are high-fidelity detections

detection_candidates.technique_name: OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
detection_candidates.rationale: high — SAM/registry-hive access and reg save of HKLM\SAM are detectable via registry-access and process-command-line telemetry
high — bursts of SMB/NTLM logon failures (Event ID 4625) from a single internal host are readily detectable
high — many accounts each seeing a single failed SMB logon from one source is a classic spray signature (4625 fan-out)
medium — RDP tunneled over web shell / Plink shows as anomalous localhost-relayed RDP and RDP sourced from a web-server host; detectable via lateral-RDP and tunnel analytics
medium — pscp/WinSCP outbound SSH to external hosts from a server, transferring .7z/.ezip/.dmp files, is detectable via egress SSH monitoring and process-network correlation

medium — mass file overwrite/deletion produces a detectable burst of file-modification and I/O; detection value is early containment, since by wipe time impact is occurring. Prioritize pre-wipe precursors (BYOVD, log clearing, VSS deletion)

medium — high-rate file encryption with extension changes and ransom-note drops is detectable via file-entropy/canary and note-creation analytics, but the fake-ransomware ruse means recovery may be impossible regardless
high — shadow-copy deletion (vssadmin/wmic/WMI) and VSS service removal are high-fidelity ransomware/wiper precursors and among the most reliable early-warning detections
medium — large sequential raw writes to physical drives / mass overwrite of file content is detectable via disk-I/O and raw-device-handle telemetry, but is concurrent with the impact itself
high — a user-mode process obtaining a raw \\.\PhysicalDrive handle and writing to the boot sector/MBR is a rare, high-fidelity destructive signal (EDR raw-disk-write analytics)
medium — abnormal stopping/removal of security and VSS services (service-state change events) is detectable, though driver-level process termination may bypass service-control logging

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — off-victim infrastructure acquisition is not observable in defender host/network logs; hunt candidate via inbound-connection geo/ASN anomaly analytics (commercial-VPN egress hitting exposed apps/RDP)
low — authentication with legitimate credentials blends with normal activity; hunt candidate via impossible-travel, off-hours logon, and RDP-from-web-shell-host correlation
low — renamed-binary masquerading evades name-based rules; hunt candidate via original-filename (PE VERSIONINFO) vs on-disk-name mismatch and known-tool hash matching
medium — self-deletion of just-created executables is detectable via file-create-then-delete sequences in EDR, but overlaps with benign cleanup
low — timestamp manipulation leaves minimal live telemetry; hunt candidate via MFT $STANDARD_INFORMATION vs $FILE_NAME timestamp divergence in forensic triage

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Embedded Payloads
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — embedded payloads are opaque until extraction; hunt candidate via static/entropy analysis of the sample rather than host log detection
medium — internal horizontal port-scanning generates detectable connection fan-out and unusual scanner-binary execution, though scan tooling is easily renamed
medium — NetBIOS name-scan bursts across a subnet and NBTscan execution are detectable, but blend with legitimate admin discovery
medium — internal SMB tool copies and downloads from consumer file-sharing sites are detectable via proxy category and internal file-write telemetry, but ride trusted transfer channels
low — reading local files/DB content is high-volume normal activity; hunt candidate via bulk-access-then-stage-then-wipe sequencing correlation
medium — a non-application process issuing bulk SQL SELECT queries against DB servers and writing large CSVs is detectable via DB audit logs and endpoint file-create telemetry
medium — accumulation of archive/CSV/.dmp files in C:\windows\temp\s\ is a detectable staging pattern via file-path monitoring

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
hunting_candidates.rationale: medium — 7zip/archive utility spawning against staged data directories is detectable via process-command-line telemetry, though archiving is common admin activity
low — a shutdown/reboot call is trivially common and only meaningful as the terminal step of a wipe chain; hunt candidate via correlation with preceding raw-disk-write/log-clear events
